summary: Guidance requested: isolate healthcheck/telemetry traffic from customer token quotas to stop opaque 429 spikes
description:
Issue summary:
VeloxMetrics reports repeated opaque 429s across interactive chat paths during overnight ingestion windows. Traffic analysis shows bursts coinciding with telemetry/healthcheck probes from their edge fleet and a spike of ephemeral worker sessions. Customer is on a dedicated pool with region-aware routing.

Impact:
- Multiple downstream product teams seeing failed requests and elevated error rates during scheduled backfills (20-40% of requests returning 429).
- Business impact: realtime features degrade during nightly jobs; customer requests degreded SLA performance.

Environment:
- Customer tier: Dedicated (reserved GPU pool).
- Regions: us-east-1 primary, eu-west-1 failover for some workers.
- Ingress: pooled proxies + HTTP/2 to origin; healthchecks originate from an orchestrator that uses short-lived credentials.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Start nightly bulk backfill with 200 concurrent worker processes from us-east orchestrator.
2) Enable telemetry agent that pings /health/edge every 10s from each worker (agent is not sticky across retries).
3) Observe spike in 429s on chat and embed endpoints within 2-5 minutes of job start.
4) Stopping the telemetry agent or reducing worker concurrency eliminates 429s within 3-5 minutes.

Artifacts / Logs provided by customer:
- Trace excerpts: request IDs rqx-ua3f, rqx-ua3g with throttle header X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 (no clear route-level header).
- Sample ingress logs show many short-lived ephemeral keys: api_key=ek-0f7* reused across different IPs.
- Grafana: tenant token consumption graph shows sudden token drain aligned with healthcheck pulses.

Customer asks: how to configure Redwood so healthchecks/telemetry do not consume customer token buckets, and best practice to isolate bulk vs interactive traffic to avoid opaque 429s?
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Initial triage by Support (Aisha). Observed matching tenant-token exhaustion pattern in our billing/quotas dashboard for VeloxMetrics account id vm-8812.
Checked rate-limiter configuration for dedicated pool: default per-tenant window + per-route windows are enabled. No explicit exclusion for /health paths currently in customer route config.
Noted ephemeral-key fanout (short-lived credentials) will create many unique API keys that each get a small token bucket and refill schedule — can amplify drain across windows.

Hypothesis: healthcheck telemetry using ephemeral credentials + HTTP/2 multiplexing + pooled proxy IP reuse causes duplicate counting across token buckets and consumes tenant-level refill credits rapidly.
Observed drift in refill schedules between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 which can create soft-throttle when geo-failover fans requests into a region mid-window.

Suggested temporary mitigation: throttle or pause telemetry agents, consolidate healthchecks to a single sticky key, or change agent to use a dedicated service account pinned to a separate route with its own quota pool.
SRE follow-up: will verify whether ingress proxy currently double-counts preflight/health endpoints when connections are proxied across IP pools. Added to internal investigation queue (INT-981).
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Thanks for the detailed logs, VeloxMetrics. We're seeing tenant-level token drain matching your timestamps. Can you temporarily disable the telemetry agent for one ingestion window to confirm reduction in 429s?
VeloxMetrics (Customer) 2026-03-10: Confirmed — disabling the agent removed the 429 spike. We'll keep it off for now while you investigate. We need guidance on permanent config changes.

Diego Morales (SRE) 2026-03-11: Initial SRE notes: two immediate configuration options are available: 1) create a dedicated route for healthcheck traffic with an isolated quota pool; 2) create a dedicated API key/service account for telemetry and put it in a low-cost, high-burst quota band. We'll test route exclusion for /health on staging first.

Diego Morales (SRE) 2026-03-11: Also seeing evidence of refill-window misalignment for ephemeral keys in us-east vs eu-west. Recommended follow-ups: align refill epoch across regions and add logic to coalesce healthcheck pulses at the ingress layer.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer accepted temporary mitigation (single sticky telemetry key) and requested our recommended config steps and an ops playbook for long-term fix.
VeloxMetrics (Customer) 2026-03-12: Please include exact API/console steps, example route policy JSON, and any potential billing impact from adding an isolated quota pool.
resolution: Mitigation implemented: recommended and guided customer to create a dedicated telemetry route and a single service API key for healthchecks. Temporary reduction of telemetry pulse rate. SRE to implement quota-exclusion option and region-refill alignment in next maintenance window.
next_steps: Support: provide step-by-step console instructions and sample route policy for isolating /health endpoints into a separate quota pool (actioned 2026-03-12).
SRE: test route-exclusion for health paths on staging and validate no double-counting via pooled proxies (target 2026-03-15).
SRE/Platform: evaluate aligning refill epoch across regions or adding tenant-level coalescing for ephemeral-key fanout (RFC to be filed).
Customer: roll out single sticky telemetry key for ingestion fleet and report 3 windows of post-change metrics.
